sentences.sentence: Sertraline is a prescription medicine used to treat depression , obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), panic disorders , posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), social anxiety disorder , and premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD).
It is sold under the brand name Zoloft , and generic sertraline is widely available.
Sertraline belongs to a group of medicines called selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors , or SSRIs.
It increases serotonin activity in the brain by blocking the reuptake of serotonin (a chemical messenger that nerve cells use to communicate) back into nerve cells, so more of it stays available.
Sertraline has only very weak effects on the reuptake of norepinephrine and dopamine, and it does not block monoamine oxidase.
Sertraline is available as tablets (25 mg, 50 mg, and 100 mg), oral solution (20 mg/mL), and capsules (150 mg and 200 mg).
Sertraline is not a controlled substance.

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: Sertraline carries a boxed warning, the FDA's most serious type of warning.

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, teenagers, and young adults in short-term studies.

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: In pooled analyses of placebo-controlled antidepressant trials covering about 77,000 adults and more than 4,500 children and teenagers, the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in people aged 24 and under was higher with an antidepressant than with placebo.

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: The risk varied considerably between different antidepressants, and it also varied by condition, with the highest rate in people being treated for depression.

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: The difference between antidepressant and placebo, per 1,000 patients treated, was:

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: It is not known whether this risk continues beyond about four months of treatment.

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: There is good evidence that antidepressants delay depression coming back in adults, and depression itself raises the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors.

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: Anyone taking sertraline should be watched closely for worsening symptoms and for new or sudden changes in mood, behavior, thoughts, or feelings, especially in the first few months of treatment and whenever the dose is changed.

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: Call your healthcare provider right away, or call 911 in an emergency, if you notice:

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: thoughts about suicide or dying, or attempts to harm yourself

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: new or worse depression, anxiety, or panic attacks

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: feeling agitated, restless, angry, or irritable

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: acting aggressive or violent, or acting on dangerous impulses

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: trouble sleeping

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: a big increase in activity or talking more than is normal for you

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: any other unusual change in behavior or mood

sentences.section_title: Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
sentences.sentence: Tell family members or caregivers which symptoms to watch for, so they can call your provider if you are not able to.

The most common sertraline side effects are nausea, diarrhea or loose stools, trouble sleeping, dry mouth, tiredness, dizziness, sleepiness, tremor, indigestion, agitation, reduced appetite, increased sweating, and sexual problems.
The table below shows how often each side effect was reported in pooled placebo-controlled trials in 3,066 adults, compared with 2,293 people taking placebo.
Some side effects were more common with particular conditions.

Sleepiness was more common in depression trials, insomnia and agitation in OCD trials, constipation and agitation in panic disorder trials, tiredness in PTSD trials, and insomnia, dizziness, tiredness, dry mouth, and a general feeling of being unwell in social anxiety disorder trials.
In PMDD trials, sleepiness, dry mouth, dizziness, tiredness, and stomach pain were more common.
In these trials, 12% of people taking sertraline stopped treatment because of a side effect, compared with 4% of people taking placebo.
The most common reasons for stopping were nausea (3%), diarrhea (2%), agitation (2%), and insomnia (2%).
SSRIs including sertraline can cause sexual problems.
In men, this can mean delayed ejaculation or being unable to ejaculate, lower sex drive, and difficulty getting or keeping an erection.
In women, it can mean lower sex drive and delayed orgasm or being unable to have an orgasm.
Changes in sex drive and sexual function can also be part of depression and anxiety themselves, so the timing of when symptoms started matters.
These numbers may underestimate how often sexual side effects happen, because people and their providers do not always raise the subject.
Tell your provider about any change in sexual function, since there may be ways to manage it.
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to sertraline: rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing.
Call your doctor at once if you have:

signs of serotonin syndrome , which can be life threatening: agitation, hallucinations, confusion, coma or other changes in mental state, a racing heartbeat, high or low blood pressure, dizziness, heavy sweating, fever, muscle stiffness, twitching or overactive reflexes, loss of coordination, seizures, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea;
unusual bleeding or bruising , including nosebleeds, bleeding gums, blood in vomit or stools, or black tarry stools;

signs of a manic episode : greatly increased energy, severe trouble sleeping, racing thoughts, reckless behavior, unusually grand ideas, excessive happiness or irritability, or talking more or faster than usual;
seizures or convulsions ;
eye pain, changes in vision, or swelling or redness in or around the eye , which can be signs of angle-closure glaucoma (a sudden rise in pressure inside the eye);
signs of low sodium in the blood (hyponatremia) : headache, trouble concentrating or thinking, memory problems, confusion, weakness, or feeling unsteady, which can lead to falls.
Severe cases have caused hallucinations, fainting, seizures, coma, and death;
fainting, chest discomfort, or an irregular heartbeat , which can be signs of a heart rhythm problem called QTc prolongation.

sentences.subsection_title: Sertraline side effects in children and teenagers
sentences.sentence: The overall pattern of side effects in 281 children and teenagers treated with sertraline was generally similar to that seen in adults.

sentences.subsection_title: Sertraline side effects in children and teenagers
sentences.sentence: Side effects reported in at least 2% of children and teenagers, and at least twice as often as with placebo, that were not common in adults were fever, hyperkinesia (abnormally increased movement), urinary incontinence, aggression, nosebleeds, purpura (purple spots under the skin), joint pain, weight loss, muscle twitching, and anxiety.

sentences.subsection_title: Sertraline side effects in children and teenagers
sentences.sentence: Reduced appetite and weight loss have been seen with SSRIs, so height and weight should be monitored during treatment.

Less common side effects reported during studies include tachycardia (fast heartbeat), tinnitus (ringing in the ears), underactive thyroid, enlarged pupils, blurred vision, blood in the stools, swelling, unsteady walking, irritability, fever, raised liver enzymes, anaphylaxis, diabetes, high cholesterol, low blood sugar, increased appetite, joint pain, muscle spasms, poor coordination, coma, convulsions, reduced alertness, numbness, lethargy, restlessness, fainting, aggression, teeth grinding, confusion, euphoric mood, hallucination, blood in the urine, milk production from the breasts, priapism (a long-lasting erection), vaginal bleeding, wheezing, yawning, hair loss, cold sweats, skin inflammation, blistering, itching, rash, hives, bleeding, high blood pressure, and flushing.

Side effects reported after sertraline came onto the market include increased clotting times, AV block, slow heartbeat, atrial arrhythmias, QTc prolongation, ventricular tachycardia including Torsade de Pointes, breast enlargement in men, raised prolactin, irregular periods, SIADH, blindness, optic neuritis, cataract, severe liver problems including hepatitis, jaundice, and liver failure with some fatal outcomes, pancreatitis, several blood disorders, angioedema, low sodium, high blood sugar, rhabdomyolysis (muscle breakdown), lockjaw, serotonin syndrome, movement disorders including akathisia and dystonia, psychosis, bedwetting, nightmares, sudden kidney failure, pulmonary hypertension, eosinophilic pneumonia, loss of smell, photosensitivity, severe skin reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, spasm of blood vessels in the brain, and vasculitis.
This is not a complete list of side effects, and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.
You should not take sertraline if you are allergic to sertraline or any of the ingredients in it, if you take an MAOI or have taken one in the past 14 days, or if you take pimozide.
Do not take the oral solution if you take disulfiram.
To make sure sertraline is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have or have ever had:
liver problems
kidney problems
heart problems, or risk factors for a heart rhythm problem called QTc prolongation
bipolar disorder or mania
seizures or convulsions
low sodium levels in your blood
bleeding problems, or you take a medicine that thins the blood
narrow angles in the eye or glaucoma
a stroke or high blood pressure
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or become pregnant while taking sertraline.
Studies of women exposed to sertraline in the first trimester suggest no overall difference in the risk of major birth defects compared with the background rate.
Some studies have reported increases in specific defects, but those results are inconclusive.

Taking sertraline late in pregnancy may raise the risk of newborn problems that need longer hospital stays, breathing support, and tube feeding, and of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN), a serious lung problem.
Use in the month before delivery has been linked with a less than two-fold increase in the risk of postpartum hemorrhage (heavy bleeding after birth).
Stopping treatment is not automatically the safer choice.
In one study of 201 pregnant women with a history of major depression, those who stopped their antidepressant during pregnancy were more likely to relapse than those who continued.
This is a decision to make with your doctor.
Sertraline oral solution contains 12% alcohol and is not recommended during pregnancy, because there is no known safe level of alcohol exposure in pregnancy.
There is a pregnancy registry that collects information on antidepressant use in pregnancy.
You can join by calling 1-866-961-2388.
Low levels of sertraline and its breakdown products pass into breast milk.
In a pooled analysis of 53 mother and infant pairs, exclusively breastfed infants had an average of 2% of the sertraline levels measured in their mothers' blood, ranging from 0% to 15%.
No side effects were seen in those infants.
There is no information on whether sertraline affects milk production.
Talk with your doctor about the benefits of breastfeeding alongside your need for treatment.
Sertraline is approved for OCD in children aged 6 to 17 years.
It is not known to be safe and effective in children under 6, or for any other condition in this age group.

Children and teenagers taking sertraline should be monitored for worsening symptoms and suicidal thoughts, especially early in treatment and when the dose changes, and their weight and growth should be checked.
Older adults clear sertraline more slowly.
In one study, plasma clearance in people aged 65 and over was about 40% lower than in adults aged 25 to 32, so it took 2 to 3 weeks to reach steady levels rather than about 1 week.
Doctors usually start older adults at the low end of the dose range.
Older adults are also at greater risk of low sodium levels in the blood, particularly if they take diuretics (water pills) or are dehydrated.
Take sertraline exactly as prescribed, once a day, in either the morning or the evening.
Take it at around the same time each day.
Tablets and capsules can be taken with or without food.
Taking sertraline with food causes only a small increase in the amount absorbed.
Swallow capsules whole.
Do not open, crush, or chew them.
Your doctor may start you on a low dose and raise it gradually, usually no more often than once a week.
Keep taking sertraline even if you feel well, and do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
Tell any doctor or lab that you take sertraline before you have tests.
Sertraline can cause a false-positive result on urine screening tests for benzodiazepines, and this can continue for several days after you stop taking it.
A confirmatory test will tell the difference.
Store sertraline at room temperature, 68°F to 77°F (20°C to 25°C).

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: Sertraline oral solution must be diluted before you take it.

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: Do not mix it in advance.

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: Use the dropper supplied with the bottle.

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: The dropper has graduation marks for 25 mg and 50 mg only.

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: Mix your dose with 4 ounces (half a cup) of water, ginger ale, lemon or lime soda, lemonade, or orange juice only.

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: Do not mix it with any other liquid.

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: Drink it straight away.

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: A slight haze may appear after mixing, and this is normal.

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: The dropper dispenser contains dry natural rubber, a form of latex.

sentences.subsection_title: How to take sertraline oral solution
sentences.sentence: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you have a latex allergy.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: The usual starting dose of sertraline is 25 mg or 50 mg once a day, depending on the condition being treated, and the usual treatment range is 50 mg to 200 mg a day.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: The maximum dose for most conditions is 200 mg a day.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: If the starting dose is not enough, the dose can be raised in steps of 25 mg to 50 mg a day.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: Because sertraline stays in the body for about 24 hours, doses are usually changed no more often than once a week.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: Dosing for PMDD.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: Sertraline can be taken every day of the menstrual cycle, or only during the luteal phase, meaning you start 14 days before your period is due and continue until it starts, then repeat with each cycle.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: On daily dosing, the dose can go up by 50 mg per cycle to a maximum of 150 mg a day.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: On luteal phase dosing, the maximum is 100 mg a day, taken as 50 mg for the first 3 days of the dosing cycle and 100 mg for the rest of it.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: Sertraline 150 mg and 200 mg capsules.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: These are not used to start treatment or to titrate a dose, because there are no lower capsule strengths.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: They can be started in someone who has been taking 100 mg or 125 mg of another sertraline product for at least a week.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: The recommended capsule dose is 150 mg or 200 mg once a day, and the maximum is 200 mg a day.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: Because the dose cannot be lowered in steps using capsules alone, coming off treatment requires switching back to another sertraline product.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: Liver problems.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: With sertraline tablets and oral solution, mild liver impairment (Child-Pugh score 5 or 6) means both the starting dose and the usual range are halved, and use is not recommended in moderate or severe liver impairment (Child-Pugh score 7 to 15).

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: Sertraline capsules are not recommended in mild, moderate, or severe liver impairment, because the dose cannot be adjusted with the strengths available.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: Kidney problems.

sentences.section_title: What is the usual sertraline dosage?
sentences.sentence: No dose change is needed for mild, moderate, or severe kidney impairment, including in people on dialysis.

sentences.section_title: What happens if I miss a dose?
sentences.sentence: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember.

sentences.section_title: What happens if I miss a dose?
sentences.sentence: If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the one you missed and take the next dose at the usual time.

sentences.section_title: What happens if I miss a dose?
sentences.sentence: Do not take two doses at once.
Seek emergency medical attention or call the Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222.
Effects reported after a sertraline tablet overdose include seizures, which may be delayed, and changes in mental state including coma.
Heart effects can also be delayed and include changes in the electrical activity of the heart (QRS and QTc prolongation).
High blood pressure is seen most often, and low blood pressure is rare, though it can happen when other substances including alcohol have also been taken.
Serotonin syndrome can occur, and the risk is higher when several drugs that raise serotonin have been taken together.

sentences.section_title: What should I avoid while taking sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Do not drink alcohol while you take sertraline.

sentences.section_title: What should I avoid while taking sertraline?
sentences.sentence: In healthy volunteers, sertraline did not add to the immediate effects of alcohol on thinking and coordination, but drinking is still not recommended during treatment.

sentences.section_title: What should I avoid while taking sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how sertraline affects you.

sentences.section_title: What should I avoid while taking sertraline?
sentences.sentence: It can cause sleepiness and can affect your ability to think clearly, make decisions, or react quickly.

sentences.section_title: What should I avoid while taking sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Do not start or stop any other medicine without checking first , including over-the-counter products, vitamins, and herbal supplements.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Several medicines interact with sertraline.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Give a full list of everything you take to any provider who treats you.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: The most important interactions are:

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: MAOIs.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Taking sertraline with an MAOI raises the risk of serotonin syndrome, and the combination is contraindicated.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Examples include selegiline, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid, phenelzine, linezolid, and methylene blue.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Pimozide.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Sertraline raises pimozide levels, which can lead to QTc prolongation and irregular heartbeats.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: The combination is contraindicated.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Other medicines that raise serotonin.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: These add to the risk of serotonin syndrome.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Examples include other SSRIs and SNRIs, triptans for migraine, tricyclic antidepressants, opioids, lithium, tryptophan, buspirone, amphetamines, and St. John's wort.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Blood thinners and antiplatelet medicines.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Aspirin, clopidogrel, heparin, and warfarin can add to the bleeding risk.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: If you take warfarin, your INR should be monitored carefully.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Medicines broken down by CYP2D6.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Sertraline blocks this liver enzyme, so levels of these drugs can rise and doses may need to be lowered.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Examples include propafenone, flecainide, atomoxetine, desipramine, dextromethorphan, metoprolol, nebivolol, perphenazine, thioridazine, tolterodine, and venlafaxine.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Phenytoin and fosphenytoin.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Sertraline can raise phenytoin levels, so levels should be checked when sertraline is started or the dose is changed.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Medicines that prolong the QTc interval.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: These should generally be avoided.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Examples include certain antipsychotics (ziprasidone, iloperidone, chlorpromazine, mesoridazine, droperidol), certain antibiotics (erythromycin, gatifloxacin, moxifloxacin, sparfloxacin), Class 1A antiarrhythmics (quinidine, procainamide), Class III antiarrhythmics (amiodarone, sotalol), and others including pentamidine, methadone, halofantrine, mefloquine, dolasetron, probucol, and tacrolimus.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Disulfiram , with the oral solution only, because of its alcohol content.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: No dose adjustment is needed when sertraline is taken with cimetidine, diazepam, lithium, atenolol, tolbutamide, digoxin, or medicines broken down by CYP3A4.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: This list is not complete.

sentences.section_title: What other drugs will affect sertraline?
sentences.sentence: Many other prescription medicines, over-the-counter products, vitamins, and herbal products can interact with sertraline.
